sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.content: Acme Robotics, Inc., headquartered in Austin, TX, operates in the industrial automation and warehouse robotics sector, designing and selling autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for mid-market warehouses. As of December 31, 2024, the company employed 420 people and served 186 active warehouse sites. For FY2024, Acme Robotics reported $52.9M in revenue, up from $38.1M in FY2023, along with a 58% gross margin, $6.2M in EBITDA, and an exiting ARR of $41.0M. Management attributes this revenue growth to expansion with existing 3PL customers and two new enterprise logos signed in Q3 FY2024. The provided excerpts lack relevant information regarding other operational or tax performance system details.

sections.title: Business & Product Overview
sections.content:
Acme Robotics, Inc. is headquartered in Austin, TX, operating in the industrial automation and warehouse robotics sector. The company designs and sells autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for mid-market warehouses and had 420 employees as of December 31, 2024. Management attributes FY2024 revenue growth to expansion with existing 3PL customers and two new enterprise logos signed in Q3 FY2024.

From a financial perspective, management reported FY2024 revenue of $52.9M, compared to $38.1M in FY2023. Additional metrics for FY2024 include a gross margin of 58%, EBITDA of $6.2M, an exit ARR of $41.0M, and 186 active warehouse sites. Tax filings show a lower gross receipts number due to revenue recognition timing differences.

sections.title: Key Risks & Diligence Findings
sections.content: Diligence findings regarding administrative and operational procedures indicate several specific risks and process gaps. Specifically, regarding Successor Determinations, there is no systematic review of completed work currently being conducted, and reliance on a knowledgeable, long-time employee to overcome the lack of controls poses a risk if that individual becomes unavailable. Additionally, operating manual instructions did not spell out current investigative fact-finding requirements, there is no back-up training for employees in the Successor area, and documentation of transactions and events is lacking, with two failing acceptance sample cases containing no evidence or documentation that fact-finding investigations had been conducted. In the Employer Debits/Billings function, although Systems Review revealed no risks and indicated all internal controls were present, Acceptance Samples identified errors in billing employers properly, though contributing factors were subsequently identified and resolved.

claims.text: No systematic review of Successor Determinations is currently being conducted.
Complete reliance on the presence of long-time employees to overcome the lack of controls poses a risk because an employee could retire, become ill or otherwise become unavailable.
Successor instructions in the operating manual did not spell out current investigative fact-finding requirements.
There is no back-up training for employees in the Successor area.
Documentation is not being recorded properly for Successor Determinations, and two failing cases contained no evidence or documentation that fact-finding investigations had been conducted.

The Systems Review conducted for Employer Debits/Billings revealed no risks and indicated that all internal controls were present, but Acceptance Samples cases identified errors in billing employers properly.
Contributing factors for the Employer Debits/Billings errors were subsequently identified, and actions have been taken to resolve this problem.
